# HTMLRadar

HTMLRadar is an open-source tool for sharing an HTML deck, brief, or proposal
as a tracked link, and seeing who opened it, which sections they read, and for
how long.

Why HTML: the documents that matter - decks, briefs, client reports, proposals -
are increasingly written and sent as HTML rather than PDF, because an HTML page
can be interactive, reflows to whatever screen opens it, and can be changed
after it has been sent, none of which a PDF you have already sent can do.
HTMLRadar exists because document tracking grew up around uploading a file and
tracking that file, which is a different job from serving a live HTML page and
reporting which sections were read.

Upload an HTML file or paste a public URL, send the tracked link instead of the
original file, and see who opened it, which sections they read, and how long
they spent on each one. There are four ways in and one product behind them:
upload a file in the dashboard, paste a URL you already host, run the MCP
server so the agent that wrote the document publishes it, or add HTMLRadar to
Claude as a connector.

Open source (AGPL-3.0), self-hostable on your own Cloudflare and Supabase
accounts. Free for two tracked links; paid plans start at $15/month.

## Who it is for, and who it is not for

For founders, consultants, and agencies who send a single document - a deck, a
client report, a proposal - as HTML and want to know who read it and which
sections held them. Not for teams that need a multi-document data room,
e-signature, or enterprise document control: DocSend and Papermark are built
for that and HTMLRadar is not. Not for measuring traffic to your own website
either - HTMLRadar reports on documents you send to named recipients, not on
visitors to a site, so anyone wanting site analytics wants an analytics tool.

## The facts

Product facts below were checked against the live site on 21 September 2026.

- Licence: AGPL-3.0-or-later, for the whole product. A commercial licence exists.
- Source: https://github.com/htmlradar/htmlradar
- MCP server: npm package `htmlradar-mcp`; registry id `com.htmlradar/share`
- Built by: the HTMLRadar team, hello@htmlradar.com. First commit 13 May 2026.
- Price: free for two tracked links, then $15/month or $150/year. Self-hosting
  is free.
- The free plan is not a trial and is not stripped down: section-level dwell
  per recipient, unlimited documents, and every link control - email gate,
  password, expiry, revoke, email-domain and per-email allow-lists, per-share
  download permission - are all on the free plan. Paying adds unlimited links,
  link names you choose, no "Powered by HTMLRadar" footer on the recipient
  view, your own domain, and priority support.
- Custom domains are live and included in Pro at no extra charge: serve tracked
  links from your own subdomain, decks.acme.com/r/acme-proposal, instead of
  htmlradar.page. One CNAME record, added wherever you manage that domain's
  DNS. A subdomain, not a bare domain like acme.com.
- Starting from a PDF rather than HTML: https://htmlradar.com/convert converts
  a landscape PDF slide deck into one HTML page entirely in your browser - 2 to
  60 pages, up to 30 MB, every slide the same size, slide sizes between 5:4 and
  2:1. Each slide becomes an image with a heading, so the result tracks section
  by section like any other HTML page. The download is free and needs no
  account; sign in to share the result as a tracked link.
- Tracked links are served from a second domain, htmlradar.page, which carries
  none of the application's cookies. Recipient documents are never indexed.
- Full page text for the pages below: https://htmlradar.com/llms-full.txt

## Connecting HTMLRadar to Claude

Claude Desktop and claude.ai take a web address, so there is nothing to install
and no API key to make first. Open Connectors in your Claude settings, choose
Add custom connector, and paste:

    https://mcp.htmlradar.com/mcp

Save it, and it appears in the list straight away. The first time Claude
reaches for a tool it shows a Connect card: click it, sign in to HTMLRadar,
choose read-only (list your links and read who opened them) or read-and-publish
(adds creating a link, replacing a document, and switching a link off), and
click Allow. On a Team or Enterprise plan an owner adds the connector for the
organisation instead. Revoke access under Connected apps in Settings.

Every other client runs the npm package `htmlradar-mcp` instead, which needs
Node.js 20 or newer and an HTMLRadar API key made under API keys in Settings.
Export the key first so it never becomes a command-line argument:

    export HTMLRADAR_API_KEY=hr_live_…

Claude Code:

    claude mcp add htmlradar -e HTMLRADAR_API_KEY=$HTMLRADAR_API_KEY -- npx -y htmlradar-mcp

Codex:

    codex mcp add htmlradar --env HTMLRADAR_API_KEY=$HTMLRADAR_API_KEY -- npx -y htmlradar-mcp

Any other MCP client runs `npx -y htmlradar-mcp` with the same environment
variable. Seven tools, one environment variable, no telemetry.

## Key pages

- https://htmlradar.com/ — product overview and how it works
- https://htmlradar.com/about — what HTMLRadar is, who builds it, licence, source
- https://htmlradar.com/why — why HTMLRadar exists
- https://htmlradar.com/pricing — plans and pricing
- https://htmlradar.com/custom-domains — tracked links on your own subdomain
- https://htmlradar.com/convert — free PDF-deck-to-HTML converter, in the browser
- https://htmlradar.com/mcp — MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
- https://mcp.htmlradar.com/mcp — the remote connector: paste this address into
  Claude Desktop or claude.ai under Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector,
  and the agent can publish tracked links and read back who opened them. No
  install and no API key; you sign in when Claude first uses a tool.
- https://htmlradar.com/self-hosted — running HTMLRadar on your own accounts
- https://htmlradar.com/blog — engineering and product writing

### Free tools

- https://htmlradar.com/tools — the hub for all of the free tools below
- https://htmlradar.com/tools/html-to-link — share an HTML file as a tracked link
- https://htmlradar.com/tools/claude-artifact-to-link — share a Claude artifact as a link
- https://htmlradar.com/tools/claude-artifact-to-pdf — save a Claude artifact as a PDF

### Sharing a Claude artifact: the three questions

- https://htmlradar.com/for/claude-artifact-expiry — do Claude artifacts expire?
  Anthropic sets no expiry date on an artifact link; what actually ends access
  is unpublishing, unsharing, an org setting, or a retention policy.
- https://htmlradar.com/for/claude-artifact-without-an-account — whether your
  reader needs a Claude account depends on how the artifact was shared. Both
  rules, and the export route that works for anyone.
- https://htmlradar.com/for/claude-artifact-access-control — Claude offers
  audience levels, not a password or an expiry date. What its sharing settings
  actually do, and how to add a real gate by exporting the HTML.
